mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.7:א: (16) Reshut—one may say the reason the Sages did not want to impose on them obligation of berachat zimun when they are by themselves is because it is not so common that they be expert in berachat zimun.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.7:ב: (17) They are obligated, etc.—and even though it was explained in s.k. 12 they do not invite zimun of men and women together, and even if they wanted because their company is not fitting—that is specifically there when the men are only two and obligation of zimun comes through combining women—for this their combination and joining together is a disgrace; not so here—it deals when there are three men besides them and there is no need at all to combine them for obligation of zimun; therefore even though women and slaves combine to fulfill their obligation through hearing from the blesser and answering berachat zimun after him—there is no disgrace in this.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.7:ג: (18) And they fulfill, etc.—for as men discharge men, so they discharge women; and see in Shulchan Aruch HaRav that his view is if women wanted to separate from the men's company and invite zimun by themselves—the permission is in their hands.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.7:ד: (19) Even though they do not understand—and see in siman 193 in Mishna Berurah s.k. 5 what he wrote there in the name of Acharonim that they also fulfill birkat hamazon through hearing from the mouth of the blesser even if they do not understand lashon kodesh; and we wrote there that nevertheless it is more proper they say after the blesser word for word silently if they can.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.8:א: (20) He invites zimun with his kind—for every androgynous is one [category], not so tumtum—as below, for perhaps when it is opened this will be found male and this female; and women do not combine with men, as above in seif 6.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.8:ב: (21) Not with men, etc.—for perhaps she is female—and it was explained in seif 6 they do not invite zimun on them; and similarly with women—for perhaps he is male and their company is not fitting, as stated.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.9:_: (22) He does not invite zimun at all—meaning even with two other tumtumim; and all the more he does not combine with men and women; and nevertheless it is obvious that with three men he can combine—for he is no worse than a woman, as stated in seif 7.

peri-megadim/part-001.txt.1:א: The waiter—Taz Berachot 47 folio 2; and Levush concludes since his way is thus—this is his fixity—see there; and it is no worse than his statement we may see in a certain place even though they did not descend from animals, as in siman 193. What the Mechaber wrote Cuthean, am ha'aretz, etc.—behold one transgressing a sin and they did not excommunicate him—combines; see siman 55 in Beit Yosef; and here seif 11; and Cuthean—even though they do not observe Shabbat—some say in public domain the law is learned, and similarly many—see Rashi Pesachim perhaps it deals with Cuthean who learned and holds everything; and nowadays like gentile; and Olat Tamid ot 2—and there it will be explained, and it requires study.
peri-megadim/part-001.txt.1:ב: And what the Mechaber wrote—a convert they invite zimun and he may bless birkat hamazon and say al shehinchalta to our forefathers—I have many thoughts on this and I will set them forth with God's help. See Tosafot Bava Batra daf 81 folio 1 s.v. lema'utei—for Rabbeinu Tam a convert does not say to our forefathers; and for R' Yitzchak author of Tosafot he may say like R' Yehuda father of a multitude of nations; and nevertheless R' Yitzchak holds to give to us he does not say—the convert only sons of Keni, etc., as proven in sugya of Makkot 19 folio 1—see there; and therefore in birkat hamazon for a convert one may say d'rabbanan—for it is written on the good land that He gave you—not to a convert; and see Hagahot Maimoniyot there who wrote so for Rashi Berachot 20 folio 2—that women have no share in the land—the same for converts; and Olat Tamid 186 folio 1—that priests and Levites had cities of refuge, etc.—implies converts do not (in Hagahot Maimoniyot and so rules—and Zohar should be Zohar); however Rambam chapter 4 of Bikkurim halacha 3—a convert brings and reads—holds more than R' Yitzchak author of Tosafot—even all converts—even though it is written that You swore to our fathers to give us—already well did the author of Sefer Lechem Yehudah write in the name of Ramban and Ran: You swore to our fathers to give us—at first the oath was to Abraham who is father to converts too to give to all his seed—even converts are his seed (whom he taught faith—Rambam chapter 1 halacha 4 of Bikkurim); but afterward when the matter rolled through sale of Joseph, Egyptian exile—it was divided only to those who left Egypt—not so in viduy ma'aser sheni Rambam ruled chapter 1 halacha 17 converts do not confess—for impossible to say that You gave us—for implies You already gave—and this is impossible. And if so perforce even for Rambam a convert is exempt from birkat hamazon—for impossible 'that He gave you' as in ma'aser sheni as stated. And behold for priests and Levites Rambam wrote the reason cities of refuge and not to our forefathers to give us—worthy to give us like converts (as Ramban and Ran wrote)—for were it not they erred with golden calf—in Bikkurim and tribe of Levi they were worthy of a portion, etc.—so too here; and more than him he says. And for what Hagahot Maimoniyot wrote Berachot 20 folio 2 there Zecherim 1 is a convert obligated in birkat hamazon—41; but for what Magen Avraham wrote in 186 it is difficult—see tractate Ma'aser Sheni chapter 5 and chapter 1 of Bikkurim halacha 4—see there Rambam and Rashba; and here one should not lengthen.
peri-megadim/part-001.txt.1:ג: And I saw for Tosafot Yom Tov in tractate Bikkurim chapter 1 halacha 4 that the land was not divided to converts—for the oath was before Abraham was called—and this he explained in his composition—until here I did not understand—for at the beginning 15 it is written thus—if so how does he read that You swore to our fathers to give us—the convert; and as Ramban wrote to give us worthy was, etc.—I have not found it now in his composition. And sugya of Makkot 19 folio 1 is difficult for Rambam—and the verse he brought 'the fruit of the land that You gave me'—I gave You money and bought it—as Sefer Lechem Yehudah for Mahar'i—see there zl; see Bava Batra chapter 7 folio 1—see there. And the verse 'and He brought us to this place and gave us this land'—is difficult to me for a convert—and it requires study for me.
peri-megadim/part-001.txt.2:_: Women—Taz—that R' Yehuda Kohen combined a woman for zimun; and Mishnah Berachot 45 folio 1 is difficult; and he answered that in zimun of ten he combined; and Mishnah in zimun of three—for it implies in Tur that R' Yehuda Kohen also for three combined; and Taz answered that Mishnah one does not invite zimun—when she blesses—it is berachat zimun—similar to idolater they invite zimun—as Rashi explained practical difference to discharge others (perhaps it was difficult to him that for combination even vegetable kezayit suffices—and here implies bread—therefore he explained thus); so too a woman thus; but for combination of three one may say they combine—for if it is a doubt why was it not asked on daf 20—this teaches he combines; and Rambam holds for combination certainly not, etc.; and Eshel Avraham; and in our chiddushim we lengthened—one may say woman with men do not combine—for their company is not fitting or promiscuity; and R' Yehuda Kohen deals with woman with her husband and son—for those reasons do not apply; and see Levush seif 6 they do not invite zimun on a woman with her husband—see there. Half-slave half-free—perhaps they invite zimun on him; and for himself see siman 589 and 689—Eshel Avraham 5—and it requires study—there it will be explained.

shaarei-teshuvah/part-001.txt.3:_: Among themselves—see in Ba'er Heitev; and see in Levush that even with her husband it is not fitting to invite zimun; and see in Eliyah Rabbah there in the name of Malbushei Yom Tov; and see in Gan HaMelech siman 71 that a great one invited zimun—he and his son-in-law and daughter—and rejected his words—see there; and see there that even to combine woman or slave for mention of the Name with ten—they never saw practiced thus; and so in Agur see there. Shulchan Aruch seif 7 in Hagahah even though they do not understand—see in Magen Avraham who brought Levush's words that even though in birkat hamazon they must understand—nevertheless berachat zimun one need not understand; and see in Eliyah Rabbah who wrote Levush came to settle Levush's difficulty who challenged from siman 193 that it states they must understand—therefore he distinguishes between birkat hamazon and berachat zimun; and the reason for the distinction there; and one may also say it deals when they bless by themselves silently—only berachat zimun requires understanding; and see in Levush the reason of Eshel Avraham who wrote they must understand among themselves silently—until here; and there is missing text here—it should read they must understand or bless by themselves silently—and that is as stated.
shaarei-teshuvah/part-001.txt.4:_: The toddlers—see in Ba'er Heitev; and see in Rabbi Yosef Karo that it is the difficulty of Yad Aharon; and Magen Avraham himself siman 458 wrote six years—as written in Choshen Mishpat siman 235 see there; and in Rabbi Yosef Karo he wrote to settle somewhat Magen Avraham's words on this.

turei-zahav/part-001.txt.1:_: The waiter who ate a kezayit—lest you say he has no fixity because he goes and comes—it teaches us.
turei-zahav/part-001.txt.6:_: Women and slaves, etc.—this is Mishnah beginning of chapter 3 who ate; and in Tur it is written that R' Yehuda Kohen would rule halacha lema'aseh to combine a woman for zimun and would bring proof from Gemara chapter ma she-hayah—whether women are obligated in birkat hamazon d'oraisa or d'rabbanan—practical difference to discharge others—from which it is obvious to him they combine—for otherwise it should require whether they combine; and Rambam responded to his words they do not combine, etc.; and it is difficult how he explains the Mishnah that women and slaves they do not invite zimun on them; and in Mordechai it is written Rabbeinu Simcha did an act to combine a woman for zimun—only there he concludes it was for mention of the Name alone and not other zimun; but R' Yehuda's words in Tur do not imply to explain thus from arrangement of his words—and the dispute that Binyamin brings on this.) And it appears one should say the Mishnah they do not invite zimun on women—means that he give them to bless on the cup of zimun—similar to 'until where does one invite zimun'—Rashi explained it refers to the blesser in zimun; and if so in combination that a man bless with them—it is possible it is permitted; and even though the general rule is with them slaves and minors—and these even for combination are forbidden—nevertheless in this matter they are equal that they not bless in zimun. And this is proven in chapter ma she-hayah that there it does not refer to zimun but without zimun—that is a woman with her husband and her husband does not know birkat hamazon and she knows—for on this the sugya there refers afterward. And on this we are in doubt there—and Rabbeinu Yehuda was precise: why is he not in doubt whether she combines for zimun of three—from which it is obvious she combines for zimun of three—only that she will not bless; and Rambam holds zimun is stricter and it is obvious even for combination it is forbidden—except to discharge her husband in berachah is lighter since he does not know—we are in doubt specifically thus. And here he brought Rambam's view—and his language that even for combination they are forbidden. And further one may say for what Beit Yosef wrote after this in this siman in the name of Kol Bo regarding minor they combine for three—specifically one—for majority of adults is required—so too for women in the Mishnah—meaning if they are the majority one man should not invite zimun for them; but to combine two men and she is third—properly she combines—so is R' Yehuda Kohen's view.

yad-ephraim/part-001.txt.1:_: In Shulchan Aruch seif 5 exempt—see in Rashi chapter 5 of Demai who wrote to explain that they do not bless on him, etc.—meaning regarding discharging others or others discharge him—18 in this they said he does not bless and does not invite zimun and they do not bless on him, etc.; but he himself is obligated to bless on him the discharger and birkat hamazon; and specifically Keriat Shema, prayer, and tefillin he is exempt—see there; and I have not seen this view mentioned in poskim.
